As I write this it was almost two years ago, in October 2018, Robert Pearce released his Traveller Geomorphs PDF, which is an amazing resource for any Science Fiction RPG, providing ready made map tiles "Geomorphs" which can be mixed and matched to create maps or map sections of starships or city building locations. While this PDF is amazing it has on fatal flaw in my eye - the PDF contain vector rendered images - which means that they are not easily editable as an image file on a computer. This made creating map layouts on a computer for uses such as a Virtual TableTop (VTT) was not easily done.

A month ago, in July 2018, he released v2.0 of the Geomorphs PDF. A week after that he released the Traveller Starship Symbols PDF. These kicked me into gear rendering these PDFs into image files which can be edited and combined to create starships and larger maps.

This archive presents the Geomorph tiles in PNG format with transparent floor backgrounds. This allows you to overlay the images on a square or hexagon grid or no grid at all (baseplates with pre-rendered grids are provided in the archive. Or you can toggle the grid, as I did in my sample maps below. These tiles are scaled to 60 pixels per 5 foot square (which I sometimes refer to as 60 dpi). This conveniently works out to 1 pixel = 1 inch, making a 1 yard hex 36 pixels across. I do have a second version of these tiles which are 5x larger (300 pixels per square). However, the file size is considerably larger and the tiles need more editing work before they can be released, so it may be a while before I release them.

About Geomorphs
---------------
"Geomorphs are deck plan tiles designed such that any number of tiles can be 
combined in multiple ways to create large, interconnect deck plans." 

Original Traveller Geomorphs PDF by Robert Pearce
http://travellerrpgblog.blogspot.com/2018/10/the-starship-geomorphs-book-if-finally.html

PNG Rendering and Custom Tiles by Eric Smith
http://gurpsland.no-ip.org/geomorphs/

About RPG Mobius Geomorphs
--------------------------
I take no credit for the amount of work put by Robert Pearce and Eric Smith for 
creating and converting the original Traveller Geomorphs. You can find their 
original work above. I strongly suggest you download Robert Pearce's PDF so you
can make sense of how these geomorphs work. All I did was write scripts that 
colorized or inverted Eric Smith's PNG rendition.

"Geomorphs are based on a 5' x 5' grid... If metric units are preferred, the 
standard 5' x 5' grid can be converted to 1.5m by 1.5m with negligible effects." 

In a 100x100 Core Geomorph lies a grid of 20x20 squares, each square is 5' x 5', 
there is a 2x2 square transparent border surrounding the geomorph for a total 
of 24x24 squares total. For metric, you can roughly round each square to 1.5m 
by 1.5m. 

I have kept most of Eric Smith instructions for Paint.Net, I have similarly 
included some instructions for Draw.io.

More information including the latest version of these files at 
http://rpgmobius.com

Using Geomorphs with Draw.io
----------------------------
Here are the settings I am using with Draw.io to create RPG content. Since 
these settings are system based, they are not saved within the files included in 
this archive.

Draw IO Settings
----------------
Extras -> Theme -> Dark

Check "Grid Size"
Check "Page View"
Check "Background"
Check "Connection Arrows"
Check "Connection Points"
Check "Guides"

I prefer working using the Dark Theme (Menus -> Extras -> Theme -> Dark), which 
sets everything in grayscale. I will often change the default color of shapes 
and objects with white (#FFFFFF), black (#000000) with shades of gray ranging 
from (#333333) to (#666666).

I strongly suggest you use several layers (Menus -> View -> Layers) and that you 
lock layers that are no longer being edited. Change Connectable property 
(Style -> Property -> Connectable) of your shapes and objects if you 
don't want them being automatically linked to one another.

I originaly used the default size of 10pt grid. But have also used a 5pt grid
as it is easier to work when accounting for standard paper size. However, as a 
default for new users working with geomorphs and VTT, I strongly suggest 15pt 
as you will not have to resize every geomorphs, you can simply drag and drop 
geomorphs in draw.io. 

Hence, a normal 100x100 Core Geomorph will exactly fit one page of 12"x 12" in 
15pt grid. While a high resolution 100x100 Core Geomorph will exactly fit one 
page of 60"x60" in 75pt grid. Note that the actual transparent border will 
overlap adjacent pages, but this is expected when putting several Geomorphs 
together.

Upon exporting (Menu -> File -> Export as PNG...), depending on the grid size 
and the virtual tabletop software you are using, you can ajust the zoom setting 
so you end up with the proper result. I'm not a fan of 70 x 70, but it is being

As I write this it was almost two years ago, in October 2018, Robert Pearce released his Traveller Geomorphs PDF, which is an amazing resource for any Science Fiction RPG, providing ready made map tiles "Geomorphs" which can be mixed and matched to create maps or map sections of starships or city building locations. While this PDF is amazing it has on fatal flaw in my eye - the PDF contain vector rendered images - which means that they are not easily editable as an image file on a computer. This made creating map layouts on a computer for uses such as a Virtual TableTop (VTT) was not easily done.

A month ago, in July 2018, he released v2.0 of the Geomorphs PDF. A week after that he released the Traveller Starship Symbols PDF. These kicked me into gear rendering these PDFs into image files which can be edited and combined to create starships and larger maps.

This archive presents the Geomorph tiles in PNG format with transparent floor backgrounds. This allows you to overlay the images on a square or hexagon grid or no grid at all (baseplates with pre-rendered grids are provided in the archive. Or you can toggle the grid, as I did in my sample maps below. These tiles are scaled to 60 pixels per 5 foot square (which I sometimes refer to as 60 dpi). This conveniently works out to 1 pixel = 1 inch, making a 1 yard hex 36 pixels across. I do have a second version of these tiles which are 5x larger (300 pixels per square). However, the file size is considerably larger and the tiles need more editing work before they can be released, so it may be a while before I release them.

About Geomorphs
---------------
"Geomorphs are deck plan tiles designed such that any number of tiles can be 
combined in multiple ways to create large, interconnect deck plans." 

Original Traveller Geomorphs PDF by Robert Pearce
http://travellerrpgblog.blogspot.com/2018/10/the-starship-geomorphs-book-if-finally.html

PNG Rendering and Custom Tiles by Eric Smith
http://gurpsland.no-ip.org/geomorphs/

About RPG Mobius Geomorphs
--------------------------
I take no credit for the amount of work put by Robert Pearce and Eric Smith for 
creating and converting the original Traveller Geomorphs. You can find their 
original work above. I strongly suggest you download Robert Pearce's PDF so you
can make sense of how these geomorphs work. All I did was write scripts that 
colorized or inverted Eric Smith's PNG rendition.

"Geomorphs are based on a 5' x 5' grid... If metric units are preferred, the 
standard 5' x 5' grid can be converted to 1.5m by 1.5m with negligible effects." 

In a 100x100 Core Geomorph lies a grid of 20x20 squares, each square is 5' x 5', 
there is a 2x2 square transparent border surrounding the geomorph for a total 
of 24x24 squares total. For metric, you can roughly round each square to 1.5m 
by 1.5m. 

I have kept most of Eric Smith instructions for Paint.Net, I have similarly 
included some instructions for Draw.io.

More information including the latest version of these files at 
http://rpgmobius.com

As I write this it was almost two years ago, in October 2018, Robert Pearce released his Traveller Geomorphs PDF, which is an amazing resource for any Science Fiction RPG, providing ready made map tiles "Geomorphs" which can be mixed and matched to create maps or map sections of starships or city building locations. While this PDF is amazing it has on fatal flaw in my eye - the PDF contain vector rendered images - which means that they are not easily editable as an image file on a computer. This made creating map layouts on a computer for uses such as a Virtual TableTop (VTT) was not easily done.

A month ago, in July 2018, he released v2.0 of the Geomorphs PDF. A week after that he released the Traveller Starship Symbols PDF. These kicked me into gear rendering these PDFs into image files which can be edited and combined to create starships and larger maps.

This archive presents the Geomorph tiles in PNG format with transparent floor backgrounds. This allows you to overlay the images on a square or hexagon grid or no grid at all (baseplates with pre-rendered grids are provided in the archive. Or you can toggle the grid, as I did in my sample maps below. These tiles are scaled to 60 pixels per 5 foot square (which I sometimes refer to as 60 dpi). This conveniently works out to 1 pixel = 1 inch, making a 1 yard hex 36 pixels across. I do have a second version of these tiles which are 5x larger (300 pixels per square). However, the file size is considerably larger and the tiles need more editing work before they can be released, so it may be a while before I release them.

About Geomorphs
---------------
"Geomorphs are deck plan tiles designed such that any number of tiles can be 
combined in multiple ways to create large, interconnect deck plans." 

Original Traveller Geomorphs PDF by Robert Pearce
http://travellerrpgblog.blogspot.com/2018/10/the-starship-geomorphs-book-if-finally.html

PNG Rendering and Custom Tiles by Eric Smith
http://gurpsland.no-ip.org/geomorphs/

About RPG Mobius Geomorphs
--------------------------
I take no credit for the amount of work put by Robert Pearce and Eric Smith for 
creating and converting the original Traveller Geomorphs. You can find their 
original work above. I strongly suggest you download Robert Pearce's PDF so you
can make sense of how these geomorphs work. All I did was write scripts that 
colorized or inverted Eric Smith's PNG rendition.

"Geomorphs are based on a 5' x 5' grid... If metric units are preferred, the 
standard 5' x 5' grid can be converted to 1.5m by 1.5m with negligible effects." 

In a 100x100 Core Geomorph lies a grid of 20x20 squares, each square is 5' x 5', 
there is a 2x2 square transparent border surrounding the geomorph for a total 
of 24x24 squares total. For metric, you can roughly round each square to 1.5m 
by 1.5m. 

I have kept most of Eric Smith instructions for Paint.Net, I have similarly 
included some instructions for Draw.io.

More information including the latest version of these files at 
http://rpgmobius.com
